messages:
Alex: Quick FYI —noticed a regression on tail latency for long sequences when KV cache is near capacity. p99 jumps ~60% during sustained traffic bursts. Anyone else see this?
Marta: saw a tiny blip in the dashboard last night, but didn't triage. Which pipeline / batch path?
Alex: continuous-batcher on A100 nodes. Kernel route sometimes falls back to slow path when we hit OOM margin on KV. Snapshot attached below.
Jon: sharing profiler snippet I grabbed during a synthetic replay (30s window):
```
timeline: 30s
requests: 1200
median latency: 46ms
p95: 218ms
p99: 486ms
p99 (under kv pressure): 760ms
oom-events: 3 (soft evict triggers)
kv-free-bytes: 0.9GB -> 0.1GB
batch-size-avg: 11 requests
avg-avg-tokens: 128
```
Jon: The interesting bit is we still form same-size batches, but kernel selection switches to the fallback code path after the soft-eviction churn. That adds ~160ms per tail request.
Perf-Bot: perf-regressions: query=continuous_batcher; window=2026-03-09T23:00..2026-03-10T01:00; metric=p99_latency; delta=+61%; tags=[kv_pressure:true,kernel_fallback:true] :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Kevin: I think the admission heuristic should be KV-aware. Right now queue admits by token budget only; it doesn't subtract expected KV working set. When free_kv < threshold we should reduce per-batch token budget and prefer smaller batches.
Marta: agreed. Proposal: compute an "admittable_tokens" = floor((free_kv_bytes - reserved_margin) / token_kv_cost) and cap batch formation to that. If admittable_tokens < min_tokens_for_path -> route to lower memory kernel or hold queue.
Elaine: question — what's our token_kv_cost? we use 40 bytes/token estimate for 16-bit quant on Llama-variant? That seems aggressive when kv fragmentation happens.
Jon: measured token KV footprint on that model: 32-36 bytes/token avg, but fragmentation bumps instantaneous to ~48 bytes/token. So add a safety multiplier (1.25).
Kevin: rough code sketch (pseudocode):
```
avail = get_kv_free_bytes() - reserved_margin
token_cost = model_token_kv_cost * frag_mult
admittable = max(0, avail // token_cost)
if admittable < min_serving_tokens:
  reject_or_hold()  # avoid kernel fallback
else:
  batch_token_target = min(request_tokens, admittable, global_token_budget)
  admit_with_batch_target(batch_token_target)
```
Marta: also we should factor in pending eviction IO — if eviction_in_flight > 0 then lower admittable by a transient factor. eviction spikes are correlated with the slow kernel fallback.
Alex: Operational ask: can we add a flag to try a conservative admission policy for 24 hours on the canary fleet? ie: reduce global batch token cap by 30% when kv_free < 1GB and observe p99.
Jon: I'll wire a canary config: `kv_admit_mode=conservative`, `safety_margin_bytes=350_000_000`, `frag_mult=1.25`, `transient_factor=0.7` and run against replay.
Perf-Bot: canary-run queued: run_id=canary-330999; start=2026-03-11T08:00:00Z; target_nodes=4; config=[kv_admit_mode:conservative]
Kevin: For queue policy, recommend implementing a tiny hold queue that delays admission by up to 12ms to allow KV eviction to complete instead of immediately admitting a large batch that will trigger fallback. That buys time and reduces tail.
Elaine: sounds good. We should also add metrics: admittable_tokens, token_cost_estimate, kv_fragmentation_ratio, admission_reason (ok/hold/reject). Add expose to console dashboards.
Marta: and alert: if admittable_tokens drops < min_serving_tokens on >3 nodes for >2m then page oncall.
Alex: Risk: this increases per-request p50 slightly because smaller batches = less amortization. But tradeoff is lower p99 and fewer kernel fallbacks. Need product signoff?
Jon: I ran a replay with conservative policy locally: p50 +4ms, p95 -12ms, p99 -120ms, fallback-events reduced from 3->0 in 30s window. I'll drop the replay logs in the ticket.
Alex: ok let's roll to canary. @Marta can you coordinate the deploy? Also add a short note in the release channel describing the config so infra knows to watch KV telemetry.
Marta: will do. Deploy scheduled in 30m.
Perf-Bot: canary-complete: run_id=canary-330999; duration=45m; p99 delta vs baseline=-38%; fallback_events=0; admittable_tokens_avg=94; note=minor p50 increase. :thumbsup:
Kevin: follow-up: we should consider integrating kernel selection prediction earlier in the admission pipeline — if we can predict kernel fallback risk we can proactively prefer smaller batch shapes that keep us on fast kernels. But that's a follow-up project.
Alex: great thread. Next steps: (1) canary config rolled (Marta), (2) metrics/dashboards added (Elaine), (3) refine token_cost model and fragmentation telemetry (Jon), (4) consider kernel-risk predictor (Kevin). Thanks.
